questions.question: In a task quota assignment model with binary variables $x_{ij}$ for agents $i$ and tasks $j$, what does $x_{ij}=1$ mean?
options: Agent $i$ has exactly $j$ tasks to do
Agent $i$ is assigned to do task $j$
Task $i$ is done before task $j$
Agent $i$ spends one hour on task $j$

questions.question: In the task quota model $\min\sum_i\sum_jc_{ij}x_{ij}$ s.t. $\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ for every task $j$, $\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$ for every agent $i$, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ ($c_{ij}$: time of agent $i$ on task $j$, $q_i$: quota of agent $i$), which requirement does the task constraint $\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ impose?
options: Agent $i$ does exactly one of the tasks $j$
Task $j$ is done by exactly one of the agents
Task $j$ is done by at least one of the agents
Each agent works on task $j$ for one hour

questions.question: In the task quota model $\min\sum_i\sum_jc_{ij}x_{ij}$ s.t. $\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ for every task $j$, $\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$ for every agent $i$, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ ($c_{ij}$: time of agent $i$ on task $j$, $q_i$: quota of agent $i$), what does the agent constraint $\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$ require of agent $i$?
options: Agent $i$ receives exactly $q_i$ of the tasks
Agent $i$ receives at most $q_i$ of the tasks
Agent $i$ works exactly $q_i$ hours in total
Task $i$ is shared among $q_i$ different agents

questions.question: A task quota model gives every task to exactly one agent ($\sum_ix_{ij}=1$) and agent $i$ exactly $q_i$ tasks ($\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$), with binary $x_{ij}$. What is required when every quota is $q_i=1$?
options: One task per agent, while some agents may stay without a task
One agent per task, while tasks may share an agent
One task per agent, so there are as many agents as tasks
Nothing changes, since quotas only limit hours

questions.question: In the task quota model $\min\sum_i\sum_jc_{ij}x_{ij}$ s.t. $\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ for every task $j$, $\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$ for every agent $i$, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ ($c_{ij}$: time of agent $i$ on task $j$, $q_i$: quota of agent $i$), what do the quotas $q_i$ control that minimizing total time alone would not?
options: How many tasks each agent does, so the workload count is spread
How many hours each agent works, making the agents' times equal
How low the total time is, since quotas always reduce it
Which agent may share a task, so large tasks can be split

questions.question: Agents A and B share tasks 1–4; for task 3, A needs 7 hours and B needs 6 hours, and $x_{ij}=1$ if agent $i$ does task $j$. Which equation ensures that task 3 is done exactly once?

Four tasks are split between agents A and B with quotas $q_A=q_B=2$; in hours, A needs $8,5,7,6$ and B needs $1,8,6,3$ for tasks 1 to 4. With $x_{ij}=1$ if agent $i$ does task $j$, which equation states agent A's workload quota?

Worker A takes $(8,5,7,6)$ hours and worker B takes $(1,8,6,3)$ hours on jobs 1–4, and each worker must receive exactly two of the four jobs; $x_{ij}=1$ if worker $i$ gets job $j$. If A handles jobs 2 and 4 and B handles jobs 1 and 3, what is the summed time?
options: 11 hours
7 hours
26 hours
18 hours

questions.question: Agents A and B must each do exactly 2 of tasks 1–4. Agent A needs $(8,5,7,6)$ hours and agent B needs $(1,8,6,3)$ hours for tasks 1–4; $x_{ij}=1$ if agent $i$ does task $j$, else $0$. Which assignment satisfies every constraint?
options: A does tasks 1, 2, 3; B does task 4
A does tasks 1, 2; B does tasks 2, 3
A does tasks 1, 4; B does tasks 2, 3
A does tasks 2, 3; B does tasks 3, 4

questions.question: Two people share chores 1–4, exactly two chores each; person A needs $(8,5,7,6)$ hours and person B $(1,8,6,3)$ hours for chores 1–4. If each chore simply goes to whoever is faster at it, which requirements are broken?
options: Only B's quota: B gets three chores, not two
Chore 3's rule: both people end up doing it
None: the faster person may take each chore
Both quotas: person A gets one chore, B three

questions.question: In the task quota model $\min\sum_i\sum_jc_{ij}x_{ij}$ s.t. $\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ for every task $j$, $\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$ for every agent $i$, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ ($c_{ij}$: time of agent $i$ on task $j$, $q_i$: quota of agent $i$), how can agent $i$'s quota be modelled with agents that each take exactly one task?
options: Use $q_i$ identical copies of agent $i$, each doing one task
Multiply all of agent $i$'s times $c_{ij}$ by its quota $q_i$
Add $q_i$ dummy tasks of zero time for agent $i$ to perform
Split every task into $q_i$ equal parts done by agent $i$

questions.question: In the task quota model $\min\sum_i\sum_jc_{ij}x_{ij}$ s.t. $\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ for every task $j$, $\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$ for every agent $i$, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ ($c_{ij}$: time of agent $i$ on task $j$, $q_i$: quota of agent $i$), what would $x_{A1}=x_{B1}=0.5$ describe, and why does the model exclude it?
options: Task 1 done twice at half time; tasks are done once
Task 1 split between A and B; each task is done whole
Task 1 left half undone; every task must be finished
Task 1 queued for both agents; only one agent waits

questions.question: In the task quota model $\min\sum_i\sum_jc_{ij}x_{ij}$ s.t. $\sum_ix_{ij}=1$ for every task $j$, $\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$ for every agent $i$, $x_{ij}\in\{0,1\}$ ($c_{ij}$: time of agent $i$ on task $j$, $q_i$: quota of agent $i$), with $\sum_iq_i$ equal to the number of tasks, what changes if each $\sum_jx_{ij}=q_i$ is relaxed to $\sum_jx_{ij}\le q_i$?
options: Agents may take fewer tasks, so the total time can fall
Tasks may be left unassigned when an agent takes fewer
Nothing: the task equations still make all quotas hold
Agents may now take more tasks than their quotas allow

questions.question: Agents A and B must each do exactly 2 of tasks 1–4. Agent A needs $(8,5,7,6)$ hours and agent B needs $(1,8,6,3)$ hours for tasks 1–4; $x_{ij}=1$ if agent $i$ does task $j$, else $0$. Which assignment minimizes the total time?
options: A: tasks 2, 4; B: tasks 1, 3; 18 hours
A: task 2; B: tasks 1, 3, 4; 15 hours
A: tasks 1, 4; B: tasks 2, 3; 28 hours
A: tasks 2, 3; B: tasks 1, 4; 16 hours

questions.question: A task quota model has 4 tasks, each to be done by exactly one agent, and two agents with quotas $q_1=3$ and $q_2=2$. Why does no assignment satisfy all constraints?
options: The larger quota of 3 exceeds half of the 4 tasks
The quotas need 5 task slots, but there are 4 tasks
Two agents cannot share 4 tasks with unequal quotas
Agent 2 would have to do some task twice in a row

questions.question: With quotas $q_A=q_B=2$ and times A $(8,5,7,6)$, B $(1,8,6,3)$ hours for tasks 1–4, the minimum-total assignment is A: tasks 2, 3 and B: tasks 1, 4 (16 hours). Which general fact about optimal quota assignments does this illustrate?
options: An optimum may give a task to the agent who is slower at it
An optimum gives every task to the agent who is faster at it
An optimum gives each agent the $q_i$ tasks it does fastest
An optimum costs the same as ignoring the quotas altogether

questions.question: Four tasks are split between agents A and B with quotas $q_A=q_B=2$; in hours, A needs $8,5,7,6$ and B needs $1,8,6,3$ for tasks 1 to 4. Both agents start at time 0 and work in parallel, each doing its own tasks one after another. Which assignment finishes all tasks earliest?
options: A: tasks 2, 4; B: tasks 1, 3; done after 11 hours
A: tasks 2, 3; B: tasks 1, 4; done after 12 hours
A: tasks 2, 3; B: tasks 1, 4; done after 16 hours
A: tasks 1, 4; B: tasks 2, 3; done after 14 hours

questions.question: Agent A must do 1 and agent B 3 of tasks 1–4; A needs $(8,5,7,6)$ hours and B needs $(1,8,6,3)$ hours for tasks 1–4. Giving each task to its faster agent yields A: task 2, B: tasks 1, 3, 4. What follows?
options: It meets both quotas, but quotas always raise the optimum
It breaks the quotas, since B is given three of the tasks
It is optimal only because the two quotas are now unequal
It meets both quotas, and no assignment can beat 15 hours
